column1: # private_paths_history_baseline.tsv -- ACCEPTED historical commits whose ADDED LINES carry a private-record path (check_private_paths.py --history).
# sha<TAB>what. NEVER the line itself: an excerpt would put the path into the tree, where the tree ratchet reds on it.
# A pushed commit's content cannot be repaired without a force-push (ruled out 08/30), so this list does not shrink; a growth is a reviewed diff.
# d30ef38c6c28 — ACCEPTED ON THE CAPTAIN'S WORD 2026-09-21, verbatim "accept saltbench"; THIS ONE
#   INSTANCE ONLY, it does not pre-accept the next. The debt is bench's and is declared as such:
#   three per-seat config-dir paths were hardcoded in a census tool's glob AND its selftest fixture,
#   merged to public main at 10:28 in #230 and REWRITTEN OUT OF THE TREE at 11:5x in #231 (e6163119).
#   Exposure declared by their author: 58 min 34 s on public main. The TREE is clean; the BLOBS are
#   permanent in public history, and a forward rewrite does not unpublish them — a force-push on a
#   protected public default branch was ruled out 08/30 and is ruled out again here. So an accepted
#   entry is the only thing that clears this arm. The stale config-dir pattern that let them through
#   is what PR #224 fixes: holding this entry would leave saltbench running the gate that missed it.
